definition: Impute means to attribute or assign blame for something to someone.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word impute. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know impute should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Historians still impute the treaty's collapse to the young interpreter, though the archives tell a messier story.
A hint merely gestures at who might be at fault — it stops far short of impute, which formally lays the blame at someone's door.
Accuse goes further than impute: imputing assigns fault, often at a distance and in writing, while accusing charges the person openly to their face.

Assign is the plain, neutral verb for allotting fault or credit — a report assigns responsibility and moves on. Impute is heavier and more suspicious: it books blame to someone's account, often on thin proof, always in the frame impute something to someone.

To pin the blame on somebody is the informal version — quick and casual, and it always takes on. Impute does the same job in formal dress: courts and historians impute a failure to a person, and the word hints the proof may be thin.

To charge someone is to declare them at fault out loud and on the record — an open accusation made to their face. Impute can work quietly, at a distance, in reports and rumors; the blame may never be spoken to the person at all.

When the town's beloved fountain cracked in its first winter, the council wanted a name to blame.
A consultant's report supplied one: it imputed the failure to Rosa Vale, the junior mason who had sealed the basin in October.
Rosa never met the consultant.
The claim reached her thirdhand, in a paragraph she was never asked to answer, resting mostly on the fact that hers was the last signature in the log.
A retired engineer read the report and bristled.
The concrete had been poured in a cold snap weeks before Rosa touched it, a detail the report never mentions.
The council quietly shelved the document, but the word stuck to her name for years, the way written blame does.
